title: qt.qml.signalhandler: Property 'onPressed' of object QQuickMouseArea_QML_94 is a signal handler. You should not call it directly.
line: Clicking items in the System Tray no longer fills the log with a 'signal handler, you should not call it directly' warning.
explanation: When the tray forwards a press to an applet (clicking a tile in the hidden items grid, or the space around a panel icon), PlasmoidItem.qml called the applet MouseArea's onPressed handler directly, because in QML the MouseArea's pressed property hides its pressed signal. Calling a signal handler like a function makes Qt log a qt.qml.signalhandler warning. The change adds a small SystemTray::emitPressed helper that emits the real pressed(QQuickMouseEvent*) signal through the meta-object, and PlasmoidItem.qml uses it, so the applet's handler (and anything else connected) runs normally without the warning.

commits.message:
applets/systemtray: emit pressed instead of calling its handler

Forwarding a press to an applet called its MouseArea's onPressed handler
directly, since the pressed property hides the signal in QML, which made
Qt log a warning on clicks. Emit the signal from C++ instead.

BUG: 494438

media.caption: Master: clicking the Vaults tile in the tray's hidden items logs the onPressed signal handler warning
With the fix: the same click opens Vaults and nothing is logged

reviews.text: Adding a C++ helper on SystemTray to emit QQuickMouseArea's shadowed pressed signal eliminates the qt.qml.signalhandler warning cleanly and fits the existing Q_INVOKABLE helper pattern in systemtray.h (stackItemBefore/stackItemAfter). The behavior is well verified (including the wasExpanded close-on-reclick case), but SystemTray::emitPressed needs runtime validation on the untyped mouseEvent pointer and should avoid the deprecated Qt 5 QGenericArgument invoke overload.
changes: Validate mouseEvent before invoking the signal in SystemTray::emitPressed (if (!mouseArea || !mouseEvent || !mouseEvent->inherits("QQuickMouseEvent")) return;), since passing a null or wrong QObject* through an untyped pointer argument causes type confusion.

Replace the legacy QGenericArgument overload of QMetaMethod::invoke with Qt 6's QMetaMethodArgument (e.g. using method.parameterMetaType(0).iface() for the QQuickMouseEvent* parameter) to avoid deprecated Qt API in new Plasma 6 code.

reviews.text: Fixes the actual source of the warning: PlasmoidItem.qml no longer calls the applet MouseArea's onPressed handler as a function and instead emits the real pressed(QQuickMouseEvent*) signal through a small Q_INVOKABLE on the SystemTray containment, which already hosts similar helpers (stackItemAfter, showPlasmoidMenu). That is cleaner than before: every connection now runs, and an applet MouseArea with no onPressed handler no longer risks a TypeError. The regression check covers the case the direct call was added for (the battery icon toggling via wasExpanded), and the before/after log captures match. Small nit: QGenericArgument with a QObject* stands in for QQuickMouseEvent*, which is fine for a single-inheritance pointer, but a one-line comment would help maintainers.
